name: אֲחִישָׁר
summary: Ahishar was one of Solomon's officials, “over the household” (1Ki 4:6), named only in the list of his princes. The name is אֲחִי “brother of, my brother” with שָׁר, the qal perfect of שִׁיר “he has sung”: “my brother has sung”, of a kind with names that say what God has done. The text writes shin (שׁ), not sin, so the name is not שַׂר “prince”. Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: The verb שִׁיר “sing” in the qal: “then sang (יָשִׁיר) Moses”.

note: BDB a.ck.bc files the name under אָח. The reading “my brother has sung” takes שָׁר as the qal perfect of שִׁיר; nothing in the verse confirms it. Whether “brother” refers to God (as is argued for other אֲחִי־ names) is not shown by scripture.
